_comment: VEX source (#1832): one statement per RUSTSEC vulnerability deny.toml ignores, i.e. one we have triaged as not affecting Pollis. scripts/oss-inventory.mjs turns these into each product's OpenVEX document (only for packages that product ships); `oss-inventory.mjs check-vex` (supply-chain.yml) fails when this file and deny.toml's ignore list disagree. `affected` is the advisory's vulnerable version range; `aliases` must include every alias the advisory lists (CVE / GHSA ids are what customers' scanners report). `justification` is an OpenVEX justification. Write `impact_statement` for a customer: what the flaw needs, and why Pollis never gives it that.

statements.impact_statement: The Marvin attack needs an attacker to time many RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decryptions. The rsa crate reaches only the Delivery Service, through jsonwebtoken, and the service signs its LiveKit tokens with HS256: it never performs an RSA decryption, so there is nothing to time.

The timing leaks are in arithmetic on secret NIST P-256/P-384 or secp256k1 keys. Pollis never creates or uses such a key: MLS runs on ML-KEM-768+X25519 with ML-DSA-44 (legacy groups X25519/Ed25519), and the Delivery Service signs tokens with HS256. crypto-bigint 0.5 is linked through elliptic-curve 0.13 but its secret-dependent paths are never called with a secret.

The flaw lets an HTTP/2 peer flood a connection with empty DATA frames. h2 0.3 is linked only into libsql's outbound client to the database, and that client offers ALPN http/1.1 only, so no HTTP/2 connection is ever negotiated. The Delivery Service's inbound listener (hyper 1.x) is built without HTTP/2.

The denial of service needs attacker-controlled XML to be parsed. In the desktop app quick-xml is reached two ways, and neither parses untrusted input: Windows notifications use only its escape function to build toast XML (no parsing), and the plist crate parses only the app's own signed Info.plist on macOS. No Pollis product parses XML from the network or from users.
